requirements.note: Inset-grouped list, newest first, one section per day headed 'Sun, Oct 25, 2026 · $222.02'. The day total sits in the header text rather than right-aligned, but it is there.
Summary card at the top: 'October 2026', $5,269.70, '86 expenses this month'. It updates on add, edit and delete.

Sheet form with amount (decimal pad), merchant, category menu of the 7 categories, date defaulting to today (Oct 27) and an optional note. Save is disabled for empty, 0, -5 and 'abc', with the message 'Enter an amount greater than zero.' A new expense appears under a 'Tue, Oct 27, 2026' header.

Tapping a row opens a pre-filled Edit Expense sheet, and saving $40.00 updated the row, day total and month total. A native trailing swipe reveals Delete, which removes the row and updates the totals.
Categories (bar-chart toolbar button) lists the month by category, largest first, with '29% of total · 16 expenses' and a progress bar. Tapping Bills pushes a day-grouped list of only Bills.
Amounts are formatted as $1,544.59. The edit and the delete were still there after relaunch.

bugs: A swiped-open Delete action stays open after you push to Categories and come back.
The row being swiped shows a stuck grey highlight while its Delete action is revealed.
tells: The 'Enter an amount greater than zero.' error shows on a fresh, empty New Expense form before the user has typed anything.
The summary card is inset more than the list sections beneath it, so their left and right edges don't line up.
The Categories button is a generic bar-chart glyph in a shared toolbar capsule; its meaning is not obvious next to +.
In the category detail list the subtitle shows the note ('work lunch') in place of the category, so it is inconsistent with the main list ('Bills · work lunch').
A.scroll: A smooth system list: slow drags track the finger, flings decelerate naturally, and there are no blank or popping rows over 240 items. The large title collapses into a blurred inline bar and comes back correctly at the top.

requirements.note: Day-grouped card list, newest first. Headers read 'Sunday, Oct 25' with the day total right-aligned, and today's group is headed 'Today'.
Dark green hero card: 'THIS MONTH / OCTOBER 2026', $5,269.70, 86 expenses, a category colour strip and a 'View category breakdown' link. It updates live.

Sheet with a large amount field (decimal pad with a Next/Done toolbar), merchant, a menu of the 7 categories, date defaulting to Oct 27 and an optional note. Save is disabled for empty, 0 and -5, with an inline hint ('greater than $0, with up to two decimal places').
Tapping a row opens a pre-filled Edit expense sheet, and saving $40.00 updated the row and totals. Swiping a row reveals a native Delete action, which removes the row and updates the totals.
A Categories tab shows the breakdown largest first, with '29.3% of spending', a coloured bar and a chevron per row. Tapping Bills pushes that month's Bills transactions, grouped by day.
US currency throughout. The edit and the delete were still there after relaunch.

bugs: The 'Expenses' large title disappears from the screen after scrolling down and back to the top, and after swiping a row. The nav bar still reports it, but the area above the card is blank until relaunch.
tells: A heavily custom-branded look: cream background, a dark green hero card, rust-orange tint and Save button, and tinted icon tiles. It reads as designed rather than system-stock, though it is consistent.
Scrolled content is cut off by a hard opaque edge under the inline nav bar, with no soft scroll-edge or blur effect.
Rows don't show the transaction's note anywhere in the list.
The list and the Categories screen each repeat the month total card, so the Categories tab largely duplicates the Activity header.
B.scroll: Smooth and native over 240 rows, with no blank or popping rows and a natural fling and rubber-band. However, after returning to the top the large title is gone, leaving an empty band above the card.

why: Both apps meet every requirement and persist correctly. A looks and behaves like a stock SwiftUI iOS app, and its only flaws are minor swipe-state glitches. B is more striking and has nicer touches (a 'Today' header, a Next/Done keyboard toolbar, one-decimal shares), but its large title visibly vanishes after scrolling, its custom styling and hard-clipped nav bar edge give it away as not system-built, and its list hides notes.
